reading.rtitle: Request for Proposal -- Invoice Approval Platform -- Vetra Group S.p.A.
paras: 1. Introduction. Vetra Group S.p.A. invites eligible suppliers to submit a proposal for an invoice approval platform for its four companies in Italy, Austria and Slovenia. This RFP is issued by Group Procurement. Bidders are required to read all sections before they submit.

2. Mandatory requirements. Proposals that do not meet the following requirements will be disqualified: customer data stored in the European Union; integration with SAP S/4HANA; support in English and Italian. Bidders are required to confirm each requirement in writing, in the table in Annex A.

3. Submission. The submission deadline is 14 November at 17:00 Central European Time. Proposals must be uploaded to the procurement portal. Proposals sent by email will not be accepted. The pricing schedule in Annex B must be completed in euros, for three years, and its format must not be changed.

4. Clarification questions. Clarification questions may be sent through the portal until 4 November. All questions and answers will be shared with every bidder, without the name of the company that asked.

5. Evaluation and award. Proposals will be scored against the following evaluation criteria: functionality (40%), total cost over three years (35%), implementation plan (15%) and references (10%). Vetra Group expects to award the contract by 15 December. Vetra Group is not required to accept the lowest offer.

listenings.text: I score about thirty bids a year, and I can tell you how most suppliers lose. Not on price. They lose on the rules. A bidder changes the format of the pricing schedule, and we have to disqualify them. Another one answers a mandatory requirement with a sentence from their brochure, and the evaluator cannot find a clear yes or no. My advice is simple. Answer in the order of the document, and repeat the number of each requirement. Write we confirm that, and then the fact. Do not write we believe, or we are one of the leading companies. And send your clarification questions early. Every bidder will see the answer, so a good question can change the whole process.

The first RFP we lost, we lost by forty minutes. The portal closed at five in the afternoon, Central European Time, and we were in Sao Paulo, reading the deadline as our local time. Our submission was perfect, and nobody ever read it. After that, we changed the whole process. On the first day, one person reads the RFP from the first page to the last and lists every mandatory requirement. On the second day, we send our clarification questions. We complete the compliance table before we write a single sentence about the product. And we upload the submission one full day before the deadline, in their time zone. Since then, we have answered eleven RFPs, and we have been disqualified zero times.
